answer: Correlated-fault slashing requires each account to lock a 400-credit stake deposit for 6 hours before auditing field data, such as a smoke plume rising above a coastal inlet or water pooled inside a rocky hollow. When multiple accounts fail the same audit check in one epoch, the slash grows with the square of the failing count. One honest agent locks 400 credits once and forfeits just 1% (4 credits) on a solo mistake, whereas 100 fakes lock 40,000 credits and forfeit 100% (all 40,000 credits) on one shared bug. This fails if an attacker runs distinct models for each fake.
